summary: @qlik/api preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated sibling payload
details: The package declares a preinstall lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style `_0xXXXX` identifiers and string-map indirection); it checks for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temporary directory, extracts it, marks it executable via `chmodSync(..., 493)`, and then invokes it with `execFileSync(bunPath, [join(D, 'math_init.js')], { cwd: D })`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB Bun-compiled module (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) obfuscated with a shuffled numeric string array and a `WV8StW` rotator. The package advertises itself as a Qlik REST API TypeScript client, which has no need for an alternate runtime or a bun-compiled sibling module. The Bun runtime is used specifically to execute code that would not run under Node, bypassing Node-only scanners. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: an unrelated runtime is fetched at install time solely to execute obfuscated code shipped in the tarball whose behavior is opaque.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
